conventions: A construct epithet naming a class of person by a body part — נְשׂוּא פָנִים (22.8) → 'the honorable man', שַׁח עֵינַיִם (22.29) → 'the humble person' — is fused into the single English adjective under rule 30, headed on the construct (rule 23), and the supplied 'the ... man/person' joins that unit under rule 46; the rectum is not marked unrepresented beside it. Both ASV Hebrew-gloss margins corroborate the fusion and decide nothing (rule 38).

A stative qal or a hiphil the ASV renders as copula + adjective — יִסְכָּן 'be profitable' (22.2), תִצְדָּק 'thou art righteous' (22.3), רָמּוּ 'high they are' (22.12), רָחֲקָה 'is far' (22.18), יִשְׂמָחוּ 'are glad' (22.19) — keeps the whole phrase in the verb's unit and heads on the adjective, which carries the lexeme (rule 44's adjective complement); the copula is never treated as rule 20's construction-supplied one.
report: Read all 30 verses end to end, including every added unit the lemma table cannot see. No construction is analysed two ways without the ASV licensing the difference.

Suffix, waw, le, ki, min, be and article buckets all differ only by what the ASV wrote: thy/thee/thine, And/But/Yet/also/so that/Then, to/for/had/unrepresented (22.19 'laugh them to scorn' is rule 40's bare object; 22.17 'do for us' writes the for), that/For/how/When/Surely.

Recurring judgments are internally consistent: every fronted question auxiliary or copula goes to the interrogative particle (22.2, 3, 4, 5, 12, 13, 15); every supplied possessive with no suffix is added (22.6, 16, 24, 27); every subordinator supplied over an asyndetic second colon is added (22.4 That, 22.11 so that, 22.23 If) while 22.14's waw takes so that; both construct epithets (22.8 nesu panim, 22.29 shach enayim) fuse into one adjective with rule 46's supplied the ... man/person; stative verbs rendered be/is/art + adjective head on the adjective (22.2, 3, 12, 18, 19).

The three BSB disagreements are convention: 22.16 and 22.29 are waws the ASV writes no connective for (rule 14), and 22.19's dative le is silenced by 'laugh them to scorn' (rule 40), where the to belongs to the idiom and not to the object relation. None is an error.

22.5's waw + ayin fused as 'Neither is there' headed on Neither is defensible under rules 35 and 50 (the alternative would head ayin on a supplied word); the note names the competitor. 22.19's head on laugh rather than scorn is a hedged tie the note records.
Nothing here generalises beyond what the contract already says; no promotion or amendment.
